structured_output.summary: Round 2 passes. All seven round-1 findings are resolved: XPP-S2-01/02/03/04/06/07 are fixed in the inspected code and XPP-S2-05 is documented as an intentional, accepted choice that does not affect run-3/4 selection under the pinned runtime path (Run._get_calibconst calls calib_constants_all_types with exp/run only; MDBUtils query is run<=N and select_doc_in_run_range filters begin<=N<=end). post_one now sets application/octet-stream on the GridFS POST, regenerates Kerberos headers per request, persists the exact response body privately plus status/safe headers before any status check or JSON parse, and rejects redirects. deploy() re-runs check_run_slots before writing, keeps the one-shot EXECUTION directory and intent-before-POST journaling. Four new DeploymentTests exercise the real deploy loop (success with id_data substitution, HTTP 500, non-JSON 200, 302) and confirm no retry and orphan evidence preservation; unit_checks.log shows 13 tests OK. completion.py and verify() now derive counts from checked data. prepare() pins the baseline snapshot to the Stage 1 admin_checks digest. The refreshed deployment_plan.json hash 0fe56e20... matches calibration_prepare.log and status.json; 8 items sum to 125830928 bytes, run=3/run_end=4, destination only cdb_prjdatpsana/jungfrau_000010, 13 prior documents unchanged, new time_sec 1793908159 differs only as expected from the superseded round-1 plan. fixture_contract.json is metadata only and references the pilot generation manifest hash. Two new low non-blocking observations (document POST Content-Type differs from psana's proven octet-stream header; status.json implementation_sha is stale). Post-deployment readback and calibrated acceptance remain pending for round 3 and are not claimed passed.

findings.evidence: Resolved. post_one adds 'Content-Type': 'application/octet-stream' when kwargs contains 'data'; DeploymentTests asserts the header on every data POST. Plan regenerated afterwards (new script_sha256 and plan hash 0fe56e20...).

Resolved. Exact response body written to a private O_EXCL file and status/safe headers saved to .http.json before wire.require on status and before response.json(); not response.is_redirect enforced. Tests cover 500, non-JSON 200 and 302 after a successful blob, confirming body preservation and stop.
Resolved. deploy passes a lambda creating a fresh KerberosTicket header set per POST; test asserts getAuthHeaders called 5 times for 1 privilege GET plus 4 POSTs.

Resolved. completion.json values now come from pilot_generation total_bytes, readback document_count, len(run1_2_files_before) and 2*len(inventory streams); verify() derives post_requests and existing_documents_unchanged and requires intent/response/http counts equal 2*len(journal).

Accepted, intentionally unchanged, documented in responses.md. Fresh time_sec/time_stamp, run_orig=0, tstamp_orig='' retained; source provenance in extpars. findings.evidence: Resolved. DeploymentTests.exercise runs calibration.deploy with patched externals and a transport that checks intent-before-POST, URL, allow_redirects, Content-Type and id_data substitution; failure variants assert stop after the blob, no journal, preserved body, excluded Set-Cookie, and FileExistsError on re-run. README documents read-only orphan reconciliation.

Resolved. prepare() requires wire.file_sha(SNAPSHOT/destination_calibration_before.json) == frozen_report('admin_checks')['destination_calibration_sha256'] before using it as baseline; key present in Stage 1 admin_checks.json (7d5cc1e5...).

Document POST uses kwargs=dict(json=doc) so requests sends Content-Type: application/json, whereas psana's proven path (MDBWebUtils.post with cc.krbheaders) sends every write, including document POSTs, with application/octet-stream. Server acceptance of application/json for the collection endpoint cannot be verified from the repository; an unexpected rejection would stop after the first GridFS blob, which the no-retry design handles safely and tests cover.
findings.requested_change: Accept as-is (recommended; no re-prepare needed) or, if a future re-prepare occurs anyway, consider matching psana's header on document POSTs. Not required for this deployment.
